speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; I see you have increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with painful urination and a history of a swollen left ankle. To understand what is happening, have you noticed any rash, fever, or eye pain recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome). The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (left ankle followed by right knee), urethritis (painful urination), recent onset in a sexually active young male, and family history of autoimmune disease is highly suggestive. I will request images to confirm joint involvement. REQUEST IMAGES: Right_knee_XRay, Left_ankle_XRay.
